name: HR-Bench
ability_definition: The ability to see details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).

task_realism.reasoning: The Fine-grained Single-instance Perception tasks (reading embedded text, identifying the color or material of small objects) resemble parts of real near-vision work, such as reading small print, checking labels, or noticing small defects. But they are framed as finding and reading a tiny region inside a huge 4K/8K scene photo. That is closer to visual search or surveillance than to close-range inspection of documents, components, instruments or specimens. The cross-instance map and chart items drift further from near-vision workplace tasks.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Inputs are static, curated, well-lit digital images with no time pressure, no consequences for errors, and no physical interaction. Real near-vision work involves variable lighting, angles, moving objects, and depth cues. Tool-augmented zoom/crop loosely resembles leaning in or using a magnifier. However, the input distribution (high-resolution photographs of large scenes) does not match what workers typically see within a few feet of themselves.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures the resolving of fine detail and small-text reading reasonably well, which is the core of the ability. It omits close-range depth and stereo judgment, fine texture and surface inspection under real optics, and sustained detailed inspection. Part of the benchmark (cross-instance map and chart reasoning) measures spatial and relational reasoning rather than acuity. Overall it covers a meaningful but partial slice.

format_match.reasoning: The output is forced multiple choice with a few options per question. Real near-vision work produces readings, defect reports, pass/fail judgments, or transcriptions without answer options to choose from. The images are real photographs, which helps somewhat, but they are artificially large scenes chosen to hide small targets rather than typical close-range work artifacts.

transferability_reasoning: HR-Bench does stress genuine fine-detail perception, especially reading small text and identifying small-object attributes, which is the central element of Near Vision. Its setup differs substantially from workplace near vision: tiny targets inside huge static photos, multiple-choice answers, a partial focus on chart and map reasoning, and no real close-range depth or physical inspection. Strong scores therefore indicate improved image-detail resolution but only moderately predict performance on real close-range inspection and reading tasks.

2025.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, inspecting high-resolution images on a screen with ordinary zoom/pan ability (the relevant population for close-range detail inspection)

2026.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce inspecting high-resolution images on a screen with the ability to zoom. This is the typical person who reads fine print, small markings and small object attributes as part of work.
